learning_objective: The learner will identify the eight parts of a metadata record from a description of how each looks, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: infographic **sim-id:** metadata-record-anatomy
**Library:** html
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Remember
**Bloom Verb:** identify
**Learning Objective:** The learner will identify the eight parts of a metadata record from a description of how each looks, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Metadata Record, Dublin Core, Keywords, Machine-Readable Metadata, and the six core field sections (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** In quiz mode the learner clicks the marker that matches a visual hint. A click is correct when it matches the marker named in the Hint column of Content. Mastery is at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. Hovering in explore mode is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) The description repeats the title. (2) The identifier is the file name. (3) Keywords and subject are the same field. **Instructional Rationale:** Identifying the parts of a record is a Remember-level task, and an illustration of a card gives each field a place. The quiz asks the learner to recognize a field by its look, which is how they will read a real record. **Content:** The illustration is a text-free flat drawing of a catalog record card. At the top is a wide bar for a title. Below it, in a column, are seven rows. The first holds a short bar and a small person icon. The second holds a short bar and a small tag icon. The third holds a block of three thin lines. The fourth holds a short bar and a small graduation-cap icon. The fifth holds a short bar and a small scales icon. The sixth holds a row of three small rounded tags. The seventh holds a short bar with a small calendar icon and a long underlined bar. The eight markers: | # | Label | Hint (describes the look, not the name) | Description | Tip | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Title | The wide bar at the top of the card. | The name of the resource, the first thing a searcher sees. | Make it specific and unique. | | 2 | Creator | The row with a short bar and a small person icon. | The person or organization responsible, the basis for credit. | Use one consistent name form. | | 3 | Subject | The row with a short bar and a small tag icon. | The topic, as specific terms from a shared list where possible. | Use more than one specific term. | | 4 | Description | The block of three thin lines. | A short summary of what the resource is and who it is for. | Use the words a searcher would type. | | 5 | Education level | The row with a short bar and a small graduation-cap icon. | The learners the resource is written for. | Use one scheme across all records. | | 6 | Rights | The row with a short bar and a small scales icon. | The license, with its version and a link. | It must match the statement on the page. | | 7 | Keywords | The row of three small rounded tags. | Free words a searcher might use, in addition to the subject. | Add everyday terms, and avoid stuffing. | | 8 | Date and identifier | The row with a small calendar icon and a long underlined bar. | When the resource was made or updated, and its permanent address. | Use an address that will not change. | **Provenance:** The parts follow the chapter sections "Metadata Record", "Dublin Core", "The Six Core Fields", and "Keywords". The illustration is synthetic, and the sim labels the card "illustrative example". **Rules:** Each hint matches exactly one marker. The illustration contains no text, so every label comes from the table above. Markers are numbered 1 to 8 in the order of the table. **Learner Activity:** 1. In explore mode the learner hovers or clicks a marker and reads its label, description, and tip. 2. In quiz mode the sim shows a hint. 3. The learner clicks the marker they think the hint describes. 4. If the first click is wrong, the sim says so and lets the learner try once more. If the second click is also wrong, the sim reveals the marker and its description. 5. After all 8 hints the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 8 hints in a shuffled order, two attempts each. Only a correct first click counts as evidence. Correct: "Correct: [label]. [Description]". First wrong click: "Not quite. Look again at the hint: [hint]". Second wrong click: "This is [label]. [Description]". The summary shows "[n] of 8 correct on the first attempt". At 7 or more it adds "You can read a metadata record." Below 7 it lists the labels of the missed parts. **Starting State:** The illustration with eight numbered markers, explore mode active, and the prompt "Hover a marker to see what it is." **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter's complete record for Watershed Basics has the fields title, creator, subject, description, education level, rights, date, language, identifier, and type, and its six core fields are title, author, subject, grade level, license, and description.
